## Columns

| Column | Deephaven type | Description | Supplied by |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `Symbol` | String | The instrument, in the library's canonical symbol form. From REST `ticker`: "The stock symbol of the company reporting earnings." | REST |
| `RawSymbol` | String | The symbol exactly as Massive sent it, on a row whose spelling the library cannot read as the dataset's class (its `Symbol` is then null); null on every other row. Present unless the session's `unreadable_symbols` is `dm.OnError.RAISE`, which fails on such a row instead. | REST |
| `ActualEps` | double | The actual earnings per share (EPS) reported by the company for the given period. | REST |
| `ActualRevenue` | double | The actual revenue reported by the company for the given fiscal period. | REST |
| `BenzingaId` | String | The identifier used by Benzinga for this record. | REST |
| `CompanyName` | String | The name of the company releasing earnings. | REST |
| `Currency` | String | The ISO 4217 currency code indicating the denomination in which the figures are reported. | REST |
| `Date` | String | The calendar date (formatted as YYYY-MM-DD) when the earnings are scheduled or were reported. | REST |
| `DateStatus` | String | Indicates whether the date of the earnings report has been confirmed. Possible values include: projected, confirmed. | REST |
| `EpsMethod` | String | The methodology of the EPS figure. Possible values are gaap (standardized financials under Generally Accepted Accounting Principles), ffo (Funds From Operations, a non-GAAP metric commonly used to assess the operating performance of REITs), and adj (adjusted, non-GAAP). | REST |
| `EpsSurprise` | double | The difference between the actual and estimated EPS. | REST |
| `EpsSurprisePercent` | double | The EPS surprise relative to the estimate, as a decimal fraction (0.75 = 75%), calculated as eps_surprise divided by the absolute value of estimated_eps. Positive is a beat and negative a miss, even when the estimate is negative. When the estimate is 0 the value is 1 or -1, and estimates near 0 give very large values. | REST |
| `EstimatedEps` | double | The analyst consensus estimate for earnings per share (EPS) for the given period. | REST |
| `EstimatedRevenue` | double | The analyst consensus estimate for the company's revenue in the given period. | REST |
| `FiscalPeriod` | String | The fiscal period for which the earnings are reported. Examples include: Q1, Q2, H1, FY. | REST |
| `FiscalYear` | long | The fiscal year in which the earnings period falls. | REST |
| `Importance` | long | A subjective indicator of the importance of the event, on a scale from 0 (lowest) to 5 (highest). | REST |
| `LastUpdated` | Instant | The timestamp (formatted as an ISO 8601 timestamp) when the record was last updated in the system. | REST |
| `Notes` | String | Additional context, commentary, or clarifying notes related to the earnings event. | REST |
| `PreviousEps` | double | The company's reported earnings per share (EPS) for the previous comparable period. | REST |
| `PreviousRevenue` | double | The company's revenue for the previous comparable fiscal period. | REST |
| `RevenueMethod` | String | The methodology of the revenue figure. Possible values are gaap (standardized financials under Generally Accepted Accounting Principles), adj (adjusted, non-GAAP figures that exclude certain items like one-time charges or divestitures), and rental (revenue specifically derived from rental operations, typically used by REITs, leasing companies, or businesses with a rental-based model). | REST |
| `RevenueSurprise` | double | The difference between the actual and estimated revenue. | REST |
| `RevenueSurprisePercent` | double | The revenue surprise relative to the estimate, as a decimal fraction (0.126 = 12.6%), calculated as revenue_surprise divided by the absolute value of estimated_revenue. Positive is a beat and negative a miss. | REST |
| `Time` | String | The time (formatted as 24-hour HH:MM:SS EST) when the earnings are scheduled or were reported. | REST |
| `TimestampInsert` | Instant | When the library received the row, as an Instant: the local clock when the REST page, flat-file block, or WebSocket frame that carried it arrived, the same for every row of one. It is not monotonic and is not Massive's own receive time; on history() rows it is the download time, and in a poll() table the latest poll's. | REST |
